subject: Deal-driven GPU inventory: sizing by model context & precision
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara@genomix.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Long-context inference for CC-Bio model — initial capacity ask

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking the time last week. We're finalizing the scope for a dedicated deployment of the CC-Bio model (attention window ~128k tokens for clinical summarization + streaming inference). We need to understand the GPU inventory you'd recommend across model precision options (fp16, int8-quant) and how the KV cache impacts per-GPU memory headroom.

High level:
- Expected Q1 steady load: 200 concurrent low-latency sessions (median 2 tokens/sec, bursts to 10 tokens/sec)
- 40% of requests will include long historical context (>=64k tokens) requiring persistent KV cache hits
- Availability requirement: 99.95%

Can you provide a short sizing sketch and preferred next steps (we have procurement timelines that would like an MSA + SOW by end of month)? Attaching a short KV profile we exported from our prototype.

Thanks,
Tara
Director of Engineering
Genomix Therapeutics

Quick ask before we size: can you confirm the 128k window is for read-heavy summarization (mostly prefix reuse) vs random access to many disparate segments? If you have a sample distribution that would help—otherwise we'll assume 70% prefix reuse which reduces effective KV working set.

Jonas — can you draft a two-tier proposal (conservative headroom vs aggressive quantization) with estimated pod counts and per-pod GPU specs? Marissa, I'll prepare an initial timeline for procurement.

Best,
Ava

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Long-context inference for CC-Bio model — initial capacity ask

Ava / team — ran the numbers against the provided KV profile and Genomix's concurrency target. Below is a compact trade-off summary (assumptions at bottom). I kept it model-specific (CC-Bio ~ 50B dense decoder).

Summary (per-GPU memory demands and pod counts for 200 concurrent sessions):

1) Conservative profile (fp16 baseline, minimal quantization, prefer headroom for model updates):
- Per-request peak KV working set (70% prefix reuse assumption): ~48 GB RAM-equivalent (after on-GPU KV packing)
- Model params (fp16): ~100 GB VRAM (50B dense -> 100 GB fp16 mapped across model sharding)
- Effective per-GPU VRAM needed w/ tensor/model sharding + KV: ~160 GB -> implies 4x A100-80GB per pod (distributed sharding) OR 2x H100-80GB with NVLink if using advanced sharded operators
- Pod design: 4x A100-80GB (headroom for spikes), target pods = 6 (active) + 1 hot spare -> reserved = 7 pods
- Notes: high cost, best latency stability, easiest from compatibility standpoint

2) Aggressive quantization profile (int8/4-bit where safe + KV offload):
- Model params (int8 equivalent): ~25–30 GB VRAM after quantization tricks (with quant-aware kernels)
- KV working set with selective offload (keep recent prefixes on GPU, older segments on NVMe/cache): ~30 GB GPU-resident + 40 GB on fast SSD (prefetching)
- Effective per-GPU VRAM needed: ~60–80 GB -> feasible with 1x H100-80GB or 1x A100-80GB per shard in a 2-shard config
- Pod design: 2x H100-80GB per pod with fast NVMe for KV offload, target pods = 4 (active) + 1 spare -> reserved = 5 pods
- Notes: lower cost, requires model validation for quant quality and engineering to enable safe KV offload

Operational considerations:
- KV cache eviction policy: tune to keep most-reused prefixes in GPU VRAM — we recommend LRU with TTL tuned to Genomix access distribution.
- Canary strategy: start with 20% traffic on quantized variant on a single pod to validate ROUGE/clinical fidelity metrics, then ramp.
- Autoscale headroom: reserve burst capacity equal to 20% of baseline pods for peak burst handling.
- SLA implication: with reserved pods above, 99.95% is achievable assuming proactive node replacement and cross-region fallback.

Estimated monthly committed spend (Rough):
- Conservative (4x A100 pods x7 reserved): ~$720k/mo (in Redwood Dedicated equivalent pricing bands)
- Aggressive quant (2x H100 pods x5 reserved): ~$420k/mo (plus one-time quant validation effort)

Action items I recommend we include in the SOW:
- Quantization validation run (test suite + evals on clinical prompts) — 2 weeks engineering support
- KV offload config and NVMe provisioning — ops time + capacity reservation
- Canary rollout plan + quality gates

Assumptions:
- 50B dense param size ~100 GB fp16; quantization yields ~3-4x model size reduction depending on technique.
- NVMe throughput availability: >= 5 GB/s sustained per pod for prefetching older KV segments.
- 70% prefix reuse (per Ava) applied to profile; if lower, KV working set grows proportionally.

I'll attach the detailed per-session memory math in the spreadsheet.

-- Jonas
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Long-context inference for CC-Bio model — initial capacity ask

Tara — thanks for the data and Jonas' analysis. To keep procurement moving, here's an itemized near-final offer we can include in the MSA/SOW draft.

Option A — Conservative (recommended if you prioritize QA risk minimization):
- Reserved: 7 pods (4x A100-80GB per pod)
- Commitment term: 12 months
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $720,000
- Included: 2 weeks setup, monthly performance review, 48-hour on-call for infra incidents

Option B — Cost-optimized (requires quant validation sign-off):
- Reserved: 5 pods (2x H100-80GB per pod + NVMe KV offload)
- Commitment term: 12 months
- Estimated monthly committed cost: $420,000 + one-time quant validation fee (~$25k)
- Included: 3-week setup (includes quant tuning and canary run), monthly quality report, 24-hour on-call for critical incidents

Next steps I suggest:
1) Genomix confirms preferred option this week so we can prepare SOW/PO timelines.
2) If you choose Option B, sign off on a quant validation scope (Jonas/Ava to own).
3) Procurement contact (looped) to start MSA review.

Ava — can you run the canary playbook and a recommended rollout schedule in parallel so we can include it in the SOW?

Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
